summary: Makio Takemura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Mie University, University of Tsukuba (~1987–2002), and Toyo University (~2002–2020).

Makio Ueno is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from Otani University in 2009. He held posts at Otani University, serving as an assistant professor (attested 2010–2012) and remaining affiliated as of 2022.
Makoto Funaoka is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Meiji University. He served as a professor at Hokkai-Gakuen University from around 1982 to 2016.

Makoto Nagai was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1904–1907). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1942) and Toyo University (~1943–1951).

Makoto Nagamura is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who attended Azabu Junior and Senior High School (~1961–1967). He served as a professor at Japan Women's University from around 1987 to 2017.

Makoto Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed doctoral studies at Waseda University (~1995–2000). Around 2003, he served as an assistant professor at Komazawa University.

Malcolm David Eckel is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his doctorate at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served as professor at Harvard (~1980–1991) and associate professor of religion at Boston University (~1991–2020).
Mamoru Tonami was a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University (~1957–1966). He held a post at Otani University from around 1972 to 1984.
Manabendu Banerjee is an Indologist who served as Co-ordinator of DSA Sanskrit at Jadavpur University (attested 2003). He also held the post of Secretary at the Asiatic Society.

Manfred Mayrhofer was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Graz under Wilhelm Brandenstein. He held posts at Würzburg (~1958–1963), Saarland (~1963–1966), Vienna (~1966–1988), and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1985–1988).
Manfred Steger is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied under Robert Aitken and at Rutgers University (~1991–1995). He held a post at RMIT University from around 2003 to 2017.
Manfred Taube was a Tibetologist who studied under Friedrich Weller from around 1952 to 1957. In 1991, he held a professorship in Central Asian studies at Leipzig University.

Manshi Kiyozawa was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Toyo University and the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa. He served as principal of Rakuhoku High School (1888) and president of Otani University (~1901–1903).
Manudeva is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied under traditional teacher Bālakṛṣṇa Pāyaguṇḍa and under Bāla Śarman Pāyaguṇḍe.

Marc Aurel Stein was an archaeologist and Indologist who earned a doctorate at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. His posts included principal of Oriental College, Lahore (~1888–1899), and Archaeological Surveyor for the Archaeological Survey of India (1904, 1910–1912).
Marc Tiefenauer is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Lausanne by 2016 under doctoral supervisor Johannes Bronkhorst, having also studied under Nahid Rouzbeh.

Marc-Henri Deroche is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Matthew T. Kapstein as well as Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, Katsumi Mimaki, Heather Stoddard, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marcel Granet was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at École Normale Supérieure under Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at EPHE (~1922–1940), INALCO (~1925–1940), and the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises (~1927–1940).

Marcel Mauss was a scholar of religious studies who studied at the University of Bordeaux (~1890–1895). He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1901–1940) and the Collège de France (1931–1942).

Marcelle Lalou was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi, Jacques Bacot, Paul Pelliot, and Jean Przyluski. She held a post at EPHE from around 1926 to 1963.
